name: Kirbinator
description: This algorithm continuously records audio into a buffer and plays slices of the buffer under the influence of various probabilities. The slices can be pitched up and down, played forwards and backwards, and panned in stereo. Key to the operation of the algorithm are two trigger inputs, the Mark input and the Trigger input. These can be the same signal, but more interesting results often arise when they're not. Typically both signals would be regular clocks, but this is by no means a requirement. The Mark input defines the slices in the audio buffer. The Trigger input tells the Kirbinator when to choose a new slice to play and to change its playback parameters. Note that playback continues with the new parameters until another Trigger is received; it doesn't, say, play one slice and then stop. However, if the Play probability is less than 100%, a new Trigger may cause the playback to stop. A trigger on the Stop input also causes playback to stop. The audio buffer is stereo, but the algorithm can be used as mono, stereo, or mono-in stereo-out, according to the routing parameters. By default the operation of the Kirbinator is completely random. However, via the 'Random seed' parameter, the behaviour can be made repeatable. Additionally, the 'Mutate' parameter allows you to smoothly blend from one set of probabilities to another. If you enable the 'Detect' parameter, the algorithm will detect transients in the incoming audio and automatically apply marks in the audio buffer. While we expect the most common use of the Kirbinator to involve sending regular clocks to its Mark and Trigger inputs, it also makes an interesting effect with more ad hoc triggers. You may also like to combine the above with the 'Feedback' parameter, which essentially turns the effect into a delay/echo.
gui_description: The display shows a waveform representation of the audio buffer. The shorter, darker line represents the current recording position. The longer line or lines show the current playback position (if any). The small checkmarks along the top of the waveform indicate the 'marks' defined by the Mark input.

input_ports.description: The Trigger signal that tells the Kirbinator when to choose a new slice to play.

input_ports.name: Stop
input_ports.description: A trigger on this input causes the currently playing slice to stop.
